name: Amaso – AI Search Visibility & GEO
author: FOSIA Ltd

sections.description:
Amaso Lite brings local SEO/GEO checks and optional AI-provider workflows into
WordPress. Review your business context, inspect answers to customer questions
and record what you changed. English is the source documentation; a short French
summary appears below.

Website: amasoai.com · Guides: AI visibility resources · Pro plans: pricing

The interface uses English source strings. A partial French catalogue covers
core navigation and common actions; untranslated strings fall back to English.
WordPress site/user language settings select the interface language.

Included in Lite

  • Keywords and local markets — no artificial Lite keyword or market quota; manual SEO ranking records are included.
  • Business Profile — quick and deep scans of supported site content, with manually validated type, location and services retained through rescans.
  • AI suggestions — local suggestions and included BYOK suggestions; provider processing is optional and billed by the provider.
  • AI citations — manual records plus on-demand and scheduled checks with your own supported provider keys. No artificial Lite monthly citation quota; provider limits, request safeguards and hosting capacity still apply.
  • Content Audit — local/full audits and included fix actions, plus BYOK AI content audit and FAQ generation. Review proposed changes and publishable content before applying them.
  • Schema and llms.txt — supported automatic/manual JSON-LD, AI metadata and public text indexes. llms.txt is an optional publication format, not a verified ranking or citation signal.
  • Crawler/referral observations — local request-based records with the measurement limits below.
  • Action plan and exports — a local work journal and CSV/JSON exports for the available datasets.
  • IndexNow — optional URL notification after explicit opt-in; off by default.

Separate Pro capabilities

The paid Amaso edition provides Autopilot, Google Search Console and GA4
integrations, Share of Voice, PDF-ready reporting and related client-reporting
features according to the active plan, and letting an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT) connect to the site and make changes for you. These are not included in Lite; the Assistant inside the WordPress admin, which reads and audits, is.
A paid subscription does not include or replace your AI-provider usage charges.
Lite’s included local and BYOK features do not require an Amaso product license.

What the measurements mean

GEO and content-audit scores are heuristic checklists of observed page signals.
They are not a measured probability of citation, a ranking factor supplied by
Google, or proof of business results. A good Google position does not guarantee
an AI citation, and a citation does not establish a conversion or sale.

Provider checks record the query, engine, time and available answer/citation
evidence. Results can differ from the provider’s consumer app and change across
queries, models and dates. Crawler logs recognize request user-agents; they do
not prove indexing or citation. First-party AI referral counters count recognized
inbound page requests, not unique visitors, qualified leads or revenue.
The plugin does not automatically attribute conversions or sales to AI.

Citation check batches and provider usage

The “Check batches this month (UTC)” counter and applicable AMASO commercial
quotas count successful keyword-and-engine check batches. One batch concerns
one keyword and one AI engine; it consumes one quota unit when at least one
query-variant result is stored. A stored result can say the site was not cited.
Several stored variants in that batch still consume only one AMASO quota unit.

A batch can make 1–5 query-variant provider requests. Retries and provider search
tools may add usage and cost. For example, five stored variants from one keyword
and one engine count as one successful batch, with separate provider usage.
AMASO’s batch counter is therefore not a count of HTTP requests or provider fees.
A failed batch with no stored variants consumes no successful-batch quota,
although provider charges may still apply.

Lite has no AMASO monthly citation-batch quota. Provider charges, provider limits,
request safeguards and hosting capacity still apply to its included BYOK checks.

Local action plan and journal

The dashboard action plan uses local configuration and saved scan findings.
Record an action’s status and a private evidence note, then recheck observable
conditions. “Reviewed” records a human review; “Verified” applies to the specific
local condition checked, not to search rankings or AI recommendations.

The journal retains the latest 100 events, including timestamps, WordPress user
IDs, task/status changes and submitted notes. Current task notes/statuses and
baseline/latest evidence are saved separately; the 100-event cap is not a cap on
all saved data. Notes are for authorized WordPress administrators and are not
automatically published in llms.txt or sent as AI prompts.

Privacy and consent

Lite has no license activation/heartbeat client or custom updater; WordPress.org
handles its plugin updates. It does make external requests for the optional
services documented below, so it is not a zero-outbound-network plugin.
Saving results locally does not mean that provider processing stays on the site.

Stored data and public output

Data is saved in the site’s WordPress database: keywords and markets, ranking
and citation records, available answer evidence, schema definitions, business
profiles and durable manual corrections, discovered public contacts/URLs,
settings, encrypted API credentials, caches, usage counters and operational
logs. The action plan also stores its evidence snapshots, private notes, user
IDs and event history. The Pro edition additionally stores data for enabled
competitor, reporting and Autopilot features.

The 404 monitor (Optimize → Redirects) records each address visitors could not find: the path without its query string, how many times, the first and last time, and the referring website’s host name only — never an IP address, user agent or cookie. Recording is rate-limited and capped, static files are ignored, and dismissing an address or adding a redirect for it removes the entry. Redirects you create are stored as a path map. The link checker (Optimize → Links) stores only the list of problem links found in its last scan. When no SEO plugin is active, the search description you (or the Assistant) set for a page is stored in the page’s own custom field and printed as a single description tag in that page’s head; with Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO or SEOPress active, Amaso writes to their field instead and prints nothing. A search title you set for a page is stored in a custom field on that page and printed as its title tag only when no SEO plugin is active. Locations (Setup → Locations) stores only the details you type for each place (name, address, phone, email, opening hours, coordinates) and the page it is linked to, and prints them as structured data on that page. Topic clusters (Optimize → Topic clusters) stores only the ids of the pages you mark as pillars; internal-link suggestions are computed from your own content and kept briefly as a temporary cache.

Every action the in-admin Assistant (Optimize → Assistant) runs is logged (which
tool, its arguments and result, the calling WordPress user, and a timestamp) so
it can be reviewed or, for the actions that support it, undone. The Assistant’s
own conversation is saved per WordPress user so it is still there next time that
admin opens the page; “Clear conversation” erases it.

Business contact details and user-entered notes can contain personal information.
Public pages, active schema, AI metadata, robots.txt and llms.txt/llms-full.txt
are readable by visitors and crawlers. Review public business details and author
display names before publishing them. The administration email is not a fallback
for a public business contact.

CSV/JSON downloads cover the datasets offered by the export tool; they are not
a complete backup of every option or private note. WordPress personal-data tools
provide the plugin’s supported site-owner export/erasure workflow, not a blanket
guarantee of legal compliance or complete portability. Include the WordPress
database in a backup when you need all settings, saved data and notes.
Data is retained by default on uninstall; an explicit removal option controls
cleanup. Review the resulting database/backup if complete removal is required.

External services

Google PageSpeed Insights: only when you click “Test speed” on a page in the technical health check. The address of that page of your site (nothing else) is sent to https://www.googleapis.com/pagespeedonline/v5/runPagespeed, which loads it and returns its speed measures (Core Web Vitals). An optional free API key you enter in Settings is sent with it. Google terms: https://developers.google.com/terms and privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Anonymous usage statistics (amasoai.com): OFF by default. Only if you tick “Send anonymous usage statistics” in Settings, Amaso sends once a week to https://amasoai.com/wp-json/gvlm/v1/usage: a random ID created on your site, the edition, plugin/WordPress/PHP versions, the site language, and per-module counters (which modules are on, how often each was used this month). Never your site address, content, keywords or personal data. Untick the box to stop it. Terms and privacy: https://amasoai.com/terms-conditions/

No inbound connections — Amaso Lite does not open a remote-access
endpoint, does not accept connections from outside clients and does not create
Application Passwords or OAuth tokens. The Assistant only works inside the
WordPress admin, for a logged-in administrator, and only calls the AI provider
you configured (see below).

IndexNow — automatic submission is OFF by default on new installs.
Existing saved choices are retained. Explicitly enable it or request a manual
submission to notify participating search engines about public URLs. After
opt-in, eligible publish/update events can submit URLs in the background.
Requests to https://api.indexnow.org/indexnow include the host, URL list,
verification key and key-file URL; the service also receives normal connection
metadata. Notification or HTTP acceptance does not guarantee crawling, indexing,
Google inclusion, AI indexing, citations or an immediate result.
IndexNow terms and website privacy information.

Google Autocomplete — used only when you click “Find real searches” (Setup
wizard, step 2, or Keywords). Amaso requests
https://suggestqueries.google.com/complete/search for up to four topic phrases
taken from your business profile or keyword list (with your city or country when
the business is local), together with your site language and country code. No
page content, no site URL and no personal data are sent; Google receives the
usual connection metadata, including your server’s IP address. Answers are kept
for a week in a WordPress transient. This is a public suggestion endpoint that
Google does not document as an API: it can change or refuse requests, and
Amaso then shows a message instead of results. Autocomplete shows what people
type; it does not provide search volume or keyword difficulty.
Google Terms of Service and
Privacy Policy.

OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini) and Perplexity — optional
bring-your-own-key (BYOK) services for supported citation checks, business
classification, suggestions, FAQ generation, the in-admin Assistant (Optimize
→ Assistant) and AI-assisted content work.
Local heuristics do not require a provider account. AI features require your
configured provider credentials and may incur that provider’s charges, rate
limits or account restrictions; free API access is not promised.

Review the provider policies and the data being submitted before choosing an AI
action or saving credentials for scheduled use. Requests can contain keywords,
questions/instructions, the site URL, business context and relevant page excerpts,
depending on the action. Public source content is still sent externally when
used in such a request. Configured citation checks can run through WP-Cron, and
a scan can use a configured provider for classification; requests are not limited
to clicking a single test button. Review schedules before adding keys and remove
credentials or disable the relevant automation to stop future provider calls.
API requests go to the selected provider using your key.

  • OpenAI: API services agreement · privacy
  • Anthropic: commercial API terms · privacy
  • Google: terms · privacy
  • Perplexity: API terms · privacy

amasoai.com (Fosia Ltd) — Upgrade requests public monthly USD catalogue
prices from https://amasoai.com/wp-json/gvlm/v1/plans when you click “Check
current prices”. The same response also carries each paid plan’s short public
description (a subtitle and what it adds); Amaso keeps it as plain text (HTML is
removed, length is capped) and shows it only on the Upgrade screen, in place of
the list bundled with the plugin. Nothing more is sent for it. Automatic price checks are OFF by default. If you explicitly
allow them on Upgrade, opening that page checks again when the last successful
check is at least 12 hours old. Failed automatic checks retry no more often
than every 15 minutes, on a later page view. No background cron is scheduled.
You can turn automatic checks off on the same page; a manual check does not
turn them on. A manual check always requests prices immediately.

The last complete valid catalogue and its check date are stored locally until
replaced or plugin data is explicitly erased. A network failure retains those
prices with a warning; bundled prices are marked as unverified references.
Legacy cached prices have no check date until the next successful request.
Only a cache-busting timestamp is attached to the request, with a generic
Amaso-Pricing user-agent. No license key, site URL or business content is sent
by this integration. The server still receives normal connection metadata,
including the requesting IP address. A price check does not activate a license,
purchase a plan, or change existing subscription charges.
Fosia Ltd: Terms & privacy.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Amaso Lite through WordPress, or upload the amaso folder.
  2. Open Amaso → Setup and review the detected business profile, public contacts and tracked queries.
  3. Run a local audit and review the action plan. Check public schema and llms output.
  4. For AI features, review the data/cost disclosures, add your own supported provider keys and review the configured schedule before starting checks.
  5. Leave IndexNow off unless you choose to submit public URLs to that service.

Minimum requirements: WordPress 6.0+, PHP 8.1+, MySQL 5.7+ or MariaDB 10.3+.
Hosting capacity, WordPress cron execution and provider availability affect runtime.
sections.faq:
Do I need an API key or a paid Amaso license?

Local scans, heuristic scores, manual records, schema and text-index generation
do not require AI keys. Included AI processing uses your own provider keys and
provider billing. Lite does not require a paid Amaso license for those features.

Can both editions be installed?

Both can be installed, but only one runtime loads. An active compatible Pro
edition takes priority over Lite; an admin notice explains the choice. The plugin
does not silently change your activation choices. Back up shared data before
changing or deleting editions.

Where is the data?

The site’s database prefix is used for geo_* tables, including keyword, ranking,
citation, schema and request records. Shared installation code can create tables
used by the other edition; table existence does not enable a Pro feature.
Profiles, corrections, credentials, caches and the private action journal also
use WordPress options. See “Stored data and public output” for export limits.

Résumé en français

Lite inclut les outils locaux, les suggestions et contrôles IA avec vos propres
clés, les audits, la génération de FAQ et les exports disponibles, sans quota
artificiel de mots-clés ou de marchés. Les frais des fournisseurs IA restent à
votre charge. IndexNow est désactivé par défaut. Les scores sont heuristiques et
ne garantissent ni classement, ni citation, ni vente. Le journal local conserve
les 100 derniers événements ; les notes restent privées dans WordPress.
Autopilot, GSC, GA4, Share of Voice et les rapports PDF relèvent de Pro.

Le compteur mensuel utilise les lots de vérification réussis : un mot-clé et un
moteur IA, avec au moins une variante enregistrée, comptent pour une unité AMASO.
Un lot peut effectuer 1 à 5 requêtes de variantes ; les nouvelles tentatives et
la recherche peuvent ajouter des frais fournisseur. Un lot sans variante
enregistrée ne consomme pas ce quota, mais peut entraîner des frais fournisseur.
Lite reste sans quota mensuel AMASO de lots de citations.
sections.changelog:
1.0.26 – 2026-10-14

  • FIXED: links to Keywords, Business Profile, SEO Rankings and other former pages (from the Dashboard, Setup and notices) opened “Sorry, you are not allowed to access this page”. They now open the right tab.
  • CHANGED: the plugin is now listed as “Amaso – AI Search Visibility & GEO” so its purpose shows in search results (same plugin, same slug, nothing to do).
  • IMPROVED: Upgrade screen: when you check current prices, the list of what each plan adds now comes from amasoai.com too, so it matches the pricing page. Without a check, the list bundled with the plugin is shown.
  • CHANGED: removed a report request handler this edition never used (it has no Reports screen).
  • FIXED: robots.txt: the AI crawler rules were written twice, and each bot named there stopped seeing your site’s own rules (for example keeping out of wp-admin and cart links). Each bot is now named once and keeps those rules; blocked bots stay blocked, and a site that discourages search engines is left alone.

1.0.25 – 2026-10-10

  • CHANGED: requires WordPress 6.2 or later.
  • CHANGED: the admin screens load their scripts and styles as files through the WordPress script and style API; translated text reaches them through wp_localize_script.
  • CHANGED: every database query goes through $wpdb->prepare(), with table names bound as identifiers.
  • FIXED: some admin styles (Assistant, Keywords, Schema, Settings and others) were not applied.
  • FIXED: when you choose to remove data on uninstall, the AI sources and missions tables are now removed too.

1.0.24 — 2026-10-04

  • CHANGED: Amaso Lite no longer includes the remote MCP server, Application-Password and OAuth connection. The Assistant inside the WordPress admin stays: it reads and audits your site and can track and pause keywords and mark pillar pages. The changes to pages (titles, descriptions, links, redirects, structured data) are made on the Amaso screens, which are all in Lite; having an assistant apply them for you is part of the separate paid edition.
  • NEW: the Dashboard opens on your week: how often AI assistants cited you in the last 7 days against the 7 before, your missions, and the three fixes worth doing now (a blocking technical problem first).
  • NEW: Visibility → Missions: choose a search you want to be recommended for; Amaso records where you start, builds a plan (on your site and across the web) and measures the result at every check, with an honest verdict (“too early”, “no change yet”, “improving”).
  • NEW: AI Citations shows the websites the assistants actually consulted for your searches (your site, reviews and directories, social and video, guides and forums, other websites), each with what to do.
  • NEW: Optimize → Technical health: what stops Google and AI assistants from reading your key pages (errors, redirects, noindex, canonical, titles, H1, phone viewport, HTTPS, image descriptions, hreflang, robots.txt, sitemap), most severe first, with the fix. Optional speed test per page through Google PageSpeed Insights, only when you click (see External services).
  • NEW: Optimize → Shop (WooCommerce): product pages missing what AI shopping answers need (price, photo, descriptions, category, reviews, identifiers), worst first. WooCommerce products are now included in every content feature.
  • NEW: Amaso panel in the block editor: the GEO score updates as you write, with a Google preview, and the search title and description can be edited there (or written with your own AI key). The classic editor keeps the meta box.
  • NEW: the Assistant has ready-made workflows (weekly review, why am I not recommended, start a mission, improve my product pages, write the missing cluster articles) and tools for AI sources, page comparison, technical and shop audits.
  • IMPROVED: after a redirect, a search title or a search description is saved, the cached copy of that page is cleared in LiteSpeed Cache, WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache or SiteGround Optimizer, so the change shows at once.
  • NEW: Redirects suggests the page an old address used to be (matching words in the address and your page titles) and redirects the confident ones in one click; addresses your own pages link to are listed first, with the page that holds the link; automatic probes are no longer recorded.
  • NEW: the Assistant can read a page, pause weak keywords and mark a pillar page, each undoable.
  • IMPROVED: internal links read pages built with Divi, Elementor and other builders as visitors see them.
  • NEW: Keywords flags single common words, pricing words and past years (each tracked keyword costs AI credit) and pauses them in one click; the setup wizard no longer pre-selects them.
  • IMPROVED: readability and accessibility: larger small text, stronger contrast, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, plain-language activity log.
  • IMPROVED: French translation of every new screen.

1.0.23 — 2026-10-03

  • NEW: “Fix these first” after setup and on the Dashboard: up to five concrete findings with the screen that fixes each.
  • NEW: optional monthly email report (off until you turn it on).
  • NEW: the Assistant can diagnose why AI assistants may not recommend you for a search, and list what to fix first.
  • NEW: MCP tools get_cluster_gaps and draft_cluster_article: a connected Claude or ChatGPT can write the articles a topic cluster is missing, saved as drafts linked to the pillar page.
  • FIX: Plugin Check errors (exception messages now escaped, a translator comment, a WordPress 6.5 function on a 6.0 minimum).
  • NEW: optional, off-by-default anonymous usage statistics (see External services).
  • FIX: the setup wizard no longer spins forever after the site scan.
  • SECURITY: request data is sanitized as soon as it is read (business profile, Schema JSON, service account, utm_source, Schema form fields).

1.0.22 — 2026-09-28

  • NEW: Setup → Locations — describe each shop, clinic or office once (address, phone, opening hours, coordinates) and link it to its page. Amaso prints that place as its own LocalBusiness structured data on that page only, refuses invalid values with a reason instead of dropping them silently, and warns when the page text does not show the details the structured data claims. The Assistant gets get_locations.
  • NEW: Search title. The Assistant can now set a page’s search title — the headline shown in Google — written into your SEO plugin’s field when you use one, or printed by Amaso when you don’t (as the whole title tag, only on themes that support title tags). Undoable, like every change.
  • IMPROVED: Settings → AI Engines → MCP now shows, in plain steps, how to connect Claude.ai or ChatGPT to your site (paste the connection URL, approve on the consent screen, switch the connector on in a chat) — the instructions used to be hidden behind the Application Password button.

1.0.21 — 2026-09-28

  • NEW: the Assistant now works with Claude, ChatGPT (OpenAI) or Gemini using your own key, remembers your conversation between visits, and every change it makes is listed under “Recent actions” with an Undo button.
  • NEW: connect Claude.ai, ChatGPT or any MCP client with a sign-in flow (OAuth) instead of an Application Password; connected apps can be disconnected at any time from Settings.
  • NEW: Optimize → Links scans your published content for broken links, in small batches so it never slows the site.
  • NEW: Optimize → Redirects — a 404 monitor (path, count and referring host only; no IP, user agent or cookie) and a redirect manager.
  • NEW: Optimize → Internal links lists published pages that nothing links to and, for each, the pages that could link to it using words already written there. Links are added one click at a time, never inside headings or existing links, and never in page-builder pages.
  • NEW: Optimize → Topic clusters — mark a pillar page and see which supporting pages link to it and which it links back to, with a one-click fix for each gap.
  • NEW: Schema → import structured data from a URL (private and local addresses are refused).
  • NEW: a fallback XML sitemap when WordPress’s own is unavailable.
  • FIX: with no SEO plugin active, a search description set by Amaso was stored but never printed in the page head. Amaso now prints a single description tag in that case only; with Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO or SEOPress active it writes to their field and prints nothing. Unfilled template values such as %%excerpt%% are never printed.
  • FIX: plain Gutenberg content was wrongly detected as built with a page builder.
  • FIX: restoring or writing content through Amaso could corrupt backslashes and accented characters in some cases.
  • FIX: uninstall now removes all of Amaso’s tables, options and saved conversations.

1.0.20 — 2026-09-27

  • NEW: Assistant tab (Amaso → Optimize → Assistant) — a chat built into Amaso’s own admin, backed by the same tools the MCP server exposes to an outside client. It runs your own configured Claude key server-side, so no external app or MCP client is needed for day-to-day questions and actions; every tool call it makes is shown in the conversation as it happens. Free, like the rest of the BYOK model.
  • NEW: MCP/Assistant can now write a full blog article draft on a topic (grounded in your real business profile, always saved as a draft — never published automatically) and can preview then apply an FAQ section to help a page’s GEO score, in the same reviewed-before-saved pattern the existing Content Audit fix flow already uses.
  • NEW: Settings → AI Engines → MCP now has a one-click “Generate an Application Password for MCP” button, a “Test connection” button that verifies the connection live from the browser, and a ready-to-copy Claude Desktop configuration snippet.
  • FIX: the MCP “Test connection” button could fail with an unrelated 401 because the browser’s own logged-in session cookies were sent alongside the Application Password, triggering WordPress’s cookie nonce check before the password was even considered.

1.0.19 — 2026-09-27

  • NEW: MCP server, off by default. Turn it on in Amaso → Settings → AI Engines and paste the connection URL into Claude, ChatGPT or any other MCP client (using a WordPress Application Password — no separate key to create). Your assistant can then read this site’s GEO score, tracked keywords, citation stats, business-page audit, site structure and real searches, and — only when you ask it to and see it happen in the conversation — track a keyword, set a page’s search description, or add structured data through the guided Schema builder. Free in both editions; nothing here is gated by plan.
  • NEW: every MCP tool call is a single, explicit, named action, validated field by field before anything runs — there is no open-ended “do whatever seems right” tool.
  • FIX: the business-pages audit occasionally returned a stale “limit” figure when serving a cached result for a smaller request than the one already cached.

1.0.18 — 2026-09-24

  • FIX: activating the plugin now schedules the weekly automated check correctly. The weekly interval was not yet registered at activation time, so the schedule silently failed while the plugin recorded a next run that did not exist.
  • SECURITY: opening the Content Audit page or the post editor no longer saves GEO scores. Scores are stored only when a post is saved, when you click “Rescan all” or “Re-analyse” (both nonce and permission checked), or by a background batch after an update.
  • SECURITY: the GEO score saved alongside a post no longer depends on an optional nonce; it reads no request input and checks that the user can edit the post.
  • IMPROVED: the Content Audit filter tabs carry a nonce.
  • IMPROVED: the AI Citations screen’s script and styles are now loaded as files through WordPress instead of inline tags; JSON-LD is printed with WordPress’s own script-tag helper.
  • FIX: the Terms & privacy link in this readme pointed to a page that does not exist.

1.0.17 — 2026-09-24

  • FIX: WordPress Plugin Check reported four errors in the guided Schema builder (a text-cleaning function WordPress discourages). They are fixed: text typed into a Schema form field is now cleaned with WordPress’s own function.
  • IMPROVED: code-quality clean-up flagged by Plugin Check, with no change in behaviour. Queries on the plugin’s own tables now state in place why they are safe, the two places that read posted data say how it is cleaned, and the requests that ask PHP for more time (asking several AI engines, scanning many pages) go through one helper instead of five copies.
  • FIX: the kinds of business offered in the guided Schema form (Restaurant, Hotel, Pharmacy…) can now be translated; they could not be extracted before.
  • FIX: on the Lite edition, Settings and the setup checklist no longer raise PHP “undefined array key” warnings (visible with WordPress debugging on) when there is no Search Console detector to describe.

1.0.16 — 2026-09-22

  • FIX: Schema Markup (“Structured data about the business is switched off”) no longer accuses your own settings when it isn’t the cause. Every check is now read from the published page itself — the one search engines and AI actually receive — so a site where Yoast SEO, Rank Math or another SEO plugin already writes the structured data is credited for it by name, instead of Amaso claiming there is none.
  • NEW: Guided Schema — add LocalBusiness, Service, Product, Event, FAQ, How-to or Software structured data by filling in a form (name, address, phone, opening hours, prices, questions and answers…), with one clear message per missing or wrong field. No JSON-LD to write, and it works whether or not an SEO plugin is also active.
  • FIX: on a page built with a page builder whose content only exists on the public site (Divi 5 and similar), Amaso now reads the published page itself for its Schema check too, instead of silently seeing nothing.

1.0.15 — 2026-09-21

  • FIX: pages built with a page builder that renders only on the public site (Divi 5, Bricks, Oxygen…) showed “0 words” and a score of 16 in Content Audit, because their content does not exist in the admin. Amaso now reads the published page as a visitor gets it (main content only, without menu, sidebar or footer), keeps the result for twelve hours and never asks more than a few pages per screen. If the server refuses to reach its own address, the page is marked “not scored: could not be read” instead of “Poor”.
  • FIX: a page that is only a grid of articles (a blog page built with a page builder), and the WooCommerce Shop page, are no longer scored or listed among your business pages: they are listings, judged through what they list.
  • FIX: on a site where Yoast SEO, Rank Math or AIOSEO writes the structured data, the homepage check no longer says “Auto-Schema is switched off”: the SEO plugin owns the schema.

1.0.14 — 2026-09-21

  • NEW: “How your site is organised” in Content Audit. Amaso now reads how WordPress serves your content: which page is the homepage, whether a Blog page lists your articles, your categories and tags, the content types your theme or plugins add, and whether tag, author and date pages can be indexed. It keeps three kinds of address apart: pages (the business), articles (your topics) and listing pages.
  • NEW: it flags what goes wrong when they are mixed up: a homepage that is only a list of latest articles, a homepage and Blog page that are the same page, articles with no listing page, articles left in the default category, tags that hold a single article, category pages with no introduction, author and date pages that repeat the Blog page, and a missing XML sitemap. A one-page site with no articles gets no findings.
  • IMPROVED: nothing is guessed. Indexing is read from Yoast SEO and Rank Math settings; with another SEO plugin it says “not readable” instead of blaming a setting it cannot see.
  • NEW: each finding becomes an Action Plan task and is marked verified once it is no longer raised.

1.0.13 — 2026-09-21

  • NEW: “What people actually search”. Amaso can show the real searches around your topics from Google Autocomplete (what people type; free, no key, in your language; a local business is asked about its city, then its country). short_description: Inspect AI citations, review WordPress content and schema, and track local evidence with optional bring-your-own-key AI tools.
description:
Amaso Lite brings local SEO/GEO checks and optional AI-provider workflows into
WordPress. Review your business context, inspect answers to customer questions
and record what you changed. English is the source documentation; a short French
summary appears below.

Website: amasoai.com · Guides: AI visibility resources · Pro plans: pricing

The interface uses English source strings. A partial French catalogue covers
core navigation and common actions; untranslated strings fall back to English.
WordPress site/user language settings select the interface language.

Included in Lite

  • Keywords and local markets — no artificial Lite keyword or market quota; manual SEO ranking records are included.
  • Business Profile — quick and deep scans of supported site content, with manually validated type, location and services retained through rescans.
  • AI suggestions — local suggestions and included BYOK suggestions; provider processing is optional and billed by the provider.
  • AI citations — manual records plus on-demand and scheduled checks with your own supported provider keys. No artificial Lite monthly citation quota; provider limits, request safeguards and hosting capacity still apply.
  • Content Audit — local/full audits and included fix actions, plus BYOK AI content audit and FAQ generation. Review proposed changes and publishable content before applying them.
  • Schema and llms.txt — supported automatic/manual JSON-LD, AI metadata and public text indexes. llms.txt is an optional publication format, not a verified ranking or citation signal.
  • Crawler/referral observations — local request-based records with the measurement limits below.
  • Action plan and exports — a local work journal and CSV/JSON exports for the available datasets.
  • IndexNow — optional URL notification after explicit opt-in; off by default.

Separate Pro capabilities

The paid Amaso edition provides Autopilot, Google Search Console and GA4
integrations, Share of Voice, PDF-ready reporting and related client-reporting
features according to the active plan, and letting an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT) connect to the site and make changes for you. These are not included in Lite; the Assistant inside the WordPress admin, which reads and audits, is.
A paid subscription does not include or replace your AI-provider usage charges.
Lite’s included local and BYOK features do not require an Amaso product license.

What the measurements mean

GEO and content-audit scores are heuristic checklists of observed page signals.
They are not a measured probability of citation, a ranking factor supplied by
Google, or proof of business results. A good Google position does not guarantee
an AI citation, and a citation does not establish a conversion or sale.

Provider checks record the query, engine, time and available answer/citation
evidence. Results can differ from the provider’s consumer app and change across
queries, models and dates. Crawler logs recognize request user-agents; they do
not prove indexing or citation. First-party AI referral counters count recognized
inbound page requests, not unique visitors, qualified leads or revenue.
The plugin does not automatically attribute conversions or sales to AI.

Citation check batches and provider usage

The “Check batches this month (UTC)” counter and applicable AMASO commercial
quotas count successful keyword-and-engine check batches. One batch concerns
one keyword and one AI engine; it consumes one quota unit when at least one
query-variant result is stored. A stored result can say the site was not cited.
Several stored variants in that batch still consume only one AMASO quota unit.

A batch can make 1–5 query-variant provider requests. Retries and provider search
tools may add usage and cost. For example, five stored variants from one keyword
and one engine count as one successful batch, with separate provider usage.
AMASO’s batch counter is therefore not a count of HTTP requests or provider fees.
A failed batch with no stored variants consumes no successful-batch quota,
although provider charges may still apply.

Lite has no AMASO monthly citation-batch quota. Provider charges, provider limits,
request safeguards and hosting capacity still apply to its included BYOK checks.

Local action plan and journal

The dashboard action plan uses local configuration and saved scan findings.
Record an action’s status and a private evidence note, then recheck observable
conditions. “Reviewed” records a human review; “Verified” applies to the specific
local condition checked, not to search rankings or AI recommendations.

The journal retains the latest 100 events, including timestamps, WordPress user
IDs, task/status changes and submitted notes. Current task notes/statuses and
baseline/latest evidence are saved separately; the 100-event cap is not a cap on
all saved data. Notes are for authorized WordPress administrators and are not
automatically published in llms.txt or sent as AI prompts.

Privacy and consent

Lite has no license activation/heartbeat client or custom updater; WordPress.org
handles its plugin updates. It does make external requests for the optional
services documented below, so it is not a zero-outbound-network plugin.
Saving results locally does not mean that provider processing stays on the site.

Stored data and public output

Data is saved in the site’s WordPress database: keywords and markets, ranking
and citation records, available answer evidence, schema definitions, business
profiles and durable manual corrections, discovered public contacts/URLs,
settings, encrypted API credentials, caches, usage counters and operational
logs. The action plan also stores its evidence snapshots, private notes, user
IDs and event history. The Pro edition additionally stores data for enabled
competitor, reporting and Autopilot features.

The 404 monitor (Optimize → Redirects) records each address visitors could not find: the path without its query string, how many times, the first and last time, and the referring website’s host name only — never an IP address, user agent or cookie. Recording is rate-limited and capped, static files are ignored, and dismissing an address or adding a redirect for it removes the entry. Redirects you create are stored as a path map. The link checker (Optimize → Links) stores only the list of problem links found in its last scan. When no SEO plugin is active, the search description you (or the Assistant) set for a page is stored in the page’s own custom field and printed as a single description tag in that page’s head; with Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO or SEOPress active, Amaso writes to their field instead and prints nothing. A search title you set for a page is stored in a custom field on that page and printed as its title tag only when no SEO plugin is active. Locations (Setup → Locations) stores only the details you type for each place (name, address, phone, email, opening hours, coordinates) and the page it is linked to, and prints them as structured data on that page. Topic clusters (Optimize → Topic clusters) stores only the ids of the pages you mark as pillars; internal-link suggestions are computed from your own content and kept briefly as a temporary cache.

Every action the in-admin Assistant (Optimize → Assistant) runs is logged (which
tool, its arguments and result, the calling WordPress user, and a timestamp) so
it can be reviewed or, for the actions that support it, undone. The Assistant’s
own conversation is saved per WordPress user so it is still there next time that
admin opens the page; “Clear conversation” erases it.

Business contact details and user-entered notes can contain personal information.
Public pages, active schema, AI metadata, robots.txt and llms.txt/llms-full.txt
are readable by visitors and crawlers. Review public business details and author
display names before publishing them. The administration email is not a fallback
for a public business contact.

CSV/JSON downloads cover the datasets offered by the export tool; they are not
a complete backup of every option or private note. WordPress personal-data tools
provide the plugin’s supported site-owner export/erasure workflow, not a blanket
guarantee of legal compliance or complete portability. Include the WordPress
database in a backup when you need all settings, saved data and notes.
Data is retained by default on uninstall; an explicit removal option controls
cleanup. Review the resulting database/backup if complete removal is required.

External services

Google PageSpeed Insights: only when you click “Test speed” on a page in the technical health check. The address of that page of your site (nothing else) is sent to https://www.googleapis.com/pagespeedonline/v5/runPagespeed, which loads it and returns its speed measures (Core Web Vitals). An optional free API key you enter in Settings is sent with it. Google terms: https://developers.google.com/terms and privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Anonymous usage statistics (amasoai.com): OFF by default. Only if you tick “Send anonymous usage statistics” in Settings, Amaso sends once a week to https://amasoai.com/wp-json/gvlm/v1/usage: a random ID created on your site, the edition, plugin/WordPress/PHP versions, the site language, and per-module counters (which modules are on, how often each was used this month). Never your site address, content, keywords or personal data. Untick the box to stop it. Terms and privacy: https://amasoai.com/terms-conditions/

No inbound connections — Amaso Lite does not open a remote-access
endpoint, does not accept connections from outside clients and does not create
Application Passwords or OAuth tokens. The Assistant only works inside the
WordPress admin, for a logged-in administrator, and only calls the AI provider
you configured (see below).

IndexNow — automatic submission is OFF by default on new installs.
Existing saved choices are retained. Explicitly enable it or request a manual
submission to notify participating search engines about public URLs. After
opt-in, eligible publish/update events can submit URLs in the background.
Requests to https://api.indexnow.org/indexnow include the host, URL list,
verification key and key-file URL; the service also receives normal connection
metadata. Notification or HTTP acceptance does not guarantee crawling, indexing,
Google inclusion, AI indexing, citations or an immediate result.
IndexNow terms and website privacy information.

Google Autocomplete — used only when you click “Find real searches” (Setup
wizard, step 2, or Keywords). Amaso requests
https://suggestqueries.google.com/complete/search for up to four topic phrases
taken from your business profile or keyword list (with your city or country when
the business is local), together with your site language and country code. No
page content, no site URL and no personal data are sent; Google receives the
usual connection metadata, including your server’s IP address. Answers are kept
for a week in a WordPress transient. This is a public suggestion endpoint that
Google does not document as an API: it can change or refuse requests, and
Amaso then shows a message instead of results. Autocomplete shows what people
type; it does not provide search volume or keyword difficulty.
Google Terms of Service and
Privacy Policy.

OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini) and Perplexity — optional
bring-your-own-key (BYOK) services for supported citation checks, business
classification, suggestions, FAQ generation, the in-admin Assistant (Optimize
→ Assistant) and AI-assisted content work.
Local heuristics do not require a provider account. AI features require your
configured provider credentials and may incur that provider’s charges, rate
limits or account restrictions; free API access is not promised.

Review the provider policies and the data being submitted before choosing an AI
action or saving credentials for scheduled use. Requests can contain keywords,
questions/instructions, the site URL, business context and relevant page excerpts,
depending on the action. Public source content is still sent externally when
used in such a request. Configured citation checks can run through WP-Cron, and
a scan can use a configured provider for classification; requests are not limited
to clicking a single test button. Review schedules before adding keys and remove
credentials or disable the relevant automation to stop future provider calls.
API requests go to the selected provider using your key.

  • OpenAI: API services agreement · privacy
  • Anthropic: commercial API terms · privacy
  • Google: terms · privacy
  • Perplexity: API terms · privacy

amasoai.com (Fosia Ltd) — Upgrade requests public monthly USD catalogue
prices from https://amasoai.com/wp-json/gvlm/v1/plans when you click “Check
current prices”. The same response also carries each paid plan’s short public
description (a subtitle and what it adds); Amaso keeps it as plain text (HTML is
removed, length is capped) and shows it only on the Upgrade screen, in place of
the list bundled with the plugin. Nothing more is sent for it. Automatic price checks are OFF by default. If you explicitly
allow them on Upgrade, opening that page checks again when the last successful
check is at least 12 hours old. Failed automatic checks retry no more often
than every 15 minutes, on a later page view. No background cron is scheduled.
You can turn automatic checks off on the same page; a manual check does not
turn them on. A manual check always requests prices immediately.

The last complete valid catalogue and its check date are stored locally until
replaced or plugin data is explicitly erased. A network failure retains those
prices with a warning; bundled prices are marked as unverified references.
Legacy cached prices have no check date until the next successful request.
Only a cache-busting timestamp is attached to the request, with a generic
Amaso-Pricing user-agent. No license key, site URL or business content is sent
by this integration. The server still receives normal connection metadata,
including the requesting IP address. A price check does not activate a license,
purchase a plan, or change existing subscription charges.
Fosia Ltd: Terms & privacy.

upgrade_notice.1.0.1: No locked/paywalled controls anywhere in the free build; unlimited keyword and market tracking.
